item.title: Harman, a Software Engineer on our AI Infrastructure team in Seattle, went from being a master’s student in New York to working as part of the backbo...
item.description:
Harman, a Software Engineer on our AI Infrastructure team in Seattle, went from being a master’s student in New York to working as part of the backbone of Google’s AI. "I work in AI Infrastructure, focusing on the software(s) that run the supply chain for Google's data centers," he explains. "It's fast-paced, and I love seeing how the systems we build directly support Google's massive AI capabilities."
Adaptability and communication are key parts of his role. "Being able to pivot, learn quickly and scale systems on the fly is a daily requirement," he says. "You're constantly collaborating. Good software is only built when the requirements are crystal clear, making effective listening one of the most crucial skills you can have as an engineer."
Harman's top tips for those interested in similar roles: 1. “Master the CS fundamentals: Get your core concepts down before worrying about the wildly complex stuff.” 2. “Build your network: Your community will support you and open doors you didn't even know existed.” 3. “If I can do it, you can do it: The biggest hurdle is often just taking that first step.”
Explore open roles at our Seattle office → https://goo.gle/4e7f4sp

item.title: At our annual Google for Brazil event, we shared updates on how we're bringing new AI tools and features to Brazil: 📍 Ask Maps is coming to Brazil ...
item.description:
At our annual Google for Brazil event, we shared updates on how we're bringing new AI tools and features to Brazil:
📍 Ask Maps is coming to Brazil in Portuguese, so you can get your questions answered conversationally with a customized map. ⚡ We're expanding Gemini in Chrome to Brazil. 📚 Students can soon study for the ENEM exam with a dedicated experience on Gemini and NotebookLM. 📅 With new agentic capabilities on AI Mode in Search, we're helping people book and manage restaurant reservations through a conversational experience.
We're also investing in providing AI training to more Brazilians by expanding the Experience AI program through a new Google.org grant, offering new scholarships for Google Career Certificates and more.
Learn more about all the announcements from Google for Brazil → https://goo.gle/4exXGg9

item.title: Since 2025, Google has provided funding to help the electrical training ALLIANCE (etA) train thousands of electrical workers and the Manufacturing Ins...
item.description:
Since 2025, Google has provided funding to help the electrical training ALLIANCE (etA) train thousands of electrical workers and the Manufacturing Institute get thousands of workers essential AI skills. To help further close the workforce gap, we’re now expanding our total skilled trades support to $50 million to help prepare more than 300,000 American workers for the jobs of tomorrow. Learn more from Ruth Porat ⬇️ Today Google announced a meaningful expansion of our skilled trades training program, including funding for training experts whose work supports 14 labor unions and 4 trade associations across welders, pipefitters, sheet metal workers, electricians, and more. The goal of the effort is to ensure workers have the state-of-the-art skills and accreditation to pursue a skilled trades career, no matter where they want to work. We launched this effort over a year ago with the electrical training ALLIANCE (etA), and I am proud that with this expansion, Google will enable paths to high-paying careers for more than 300,000 American workers across more than 20 states.
It has been inspiring to meet trainees in the program and hear their excitement about the valuable careers this enables. Building the physical infrastructure for America’s future requires significantly increasing the pipeline of skilled tradespeople across the country – a challenge that can only be addressed with collective action across the private sector, civil society, and government. Google is proud to partner with these exceptional training experts and trade organizations. Learn more: https://lnkd.in/eRZUXwQj
